content.intro: Learn passing data from views through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Passing Data from Views matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines passing data from views as part of url routing and views. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Context dictionaries; Dynamic content; Data retrieved from models; Passing collections to templates; Avoiding unnecessary database operations. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Data retrieved from models
items.text: Data retrieved from models affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Passing collections to templates
items.text: Passing collections to templates shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: Avoiding unnecessary database operations
